comparator.route: Frontiers in Medical Biology specialisation, followed by 12 EC of electives and the standard 18-EC Bachelor Project
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum accounts for 180 EC. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC foundation in cells, genetics, microbes, animal form, anatomy, physiology, disease mechanisms, mathematics, statistics and academic skills. Year 2 is a fixed 60-EC programme in biochemistry, molecular and cell biology, immunology, molecular techniques, bioethics, biomedical data science, cellular imaging/regulation, omics and a mini-thesis. The HTML table prints a dash for Data Science, while the official 2026–27 curriculum PDF assigns it 3 EC; that PDF value completes the 60-EC year and is used here. For year 3, Frontiers in Medical Biology is selected under the broad-academic-identity rule because its molecular, genomic and experimental emphasis continues the programme's named biomedical-sciences identity more broadly than the Neurobiology or Patient Oriented Research alternatives. Its 30 EC comprise Frontiers in Medical Biology 1 (12), Frontiers in Medical Biology 2 (6), Practicum Experimental Genomics (6) and a 6-EC specialisation elective, followed by 12 EC of genuine electives and an 18-EC Bachelor Project.

alternatives.label: Human biology, disease and biomedical research
alternatives.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, anatomy and physiology, immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and neuroscience with laboratory, statistical and ethical study. It reflects the compulsory VU core while UCR lacks dedicated oncology, omics and a 24-EC experimental thesis placement.
alternatives.labelReason: The official degree centres on the human body, disease mechanisms, molecular and cellular biology, microbiology, immunology, laboratory work and independent biomedical research.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Public health, disease prevention and biomedical intervention
alternatives.concept: Studies illness across body systems and populations, combining epidemiology, immunology, human physiology, health psychology, social conditions, health financing and research methods. The organising question shifts from laboratory mechanisms toward prevention and evaluation of interventions.
alternatives.labelReason: Prevention, translation to healthcare and Patient Oriented Research provide a direct basis for a population-level health and intervention programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses differ from the biomedical core route, adding sociology, health psychology, qualitative research, public economics and persuasion while reducing specialist neuroscience, anatomy and mathematical/computational methods.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Biomedical data, omics and personalised disease models
alternatives.concept: Connects cellular and physiological disease study with programming, mathematical modelling, image analysis, machine learning and neural networks. These are general UCR computational methods applied to biomedical questions, not a substitute for VU omics laboratory training or the data-analysis thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The programme's distinctive omics and systems-biology line, genome analysis, biomedical statistics, data science and personalised-treatment questions support a quantitative biomedical route.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses differ from the closest biomedical route and twelve from public health: image processing, deep learning, linear algebra, numerical methods and signal systems displace several pharmacology, neurobehavioral and clinical research elements, materially changing the analytical tools.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

routeSelection.route: Frontiers in Medical Biology specialisation, followed by 12 EC of electives and the standard 18-EC Bachelor Project
routeSelection.basis: The programme offers three named third-year specialisations. Frontiers in Medical Biology most directly continues the degree's cross-cutting molecular-cell biology, omics, systems-biology, disease-mechanism and experimental-research identity. Neurobiology narrows toward the nervous system, while Patient Oriented Research narrows toward clinical and patient-facing biomedical research.

selection.assessment: The broad closest route covers human biology, disease mechanisms and biomedical research. Direct target evidence then supports distinct public-health/intervention and biomedical-data/omics alternatives. All three form coherent 24-course curricula, pass mechanical feasibility and differ by at least four courses per side. The separately supported Neurobiology direction cannot be added after the maximum of three.

notes.text: UvA Biomedical Sciences requires a tightly integrated molecular, anatomical, physiological, microbiological, immunological, omics and laboratory sequence, followed by a formal 30-EC specialisation and an 18-EC research placement. UCR can assemble biomedical, public-health and quantitative-data programmes, but it does not duplicate the full wet-lab sequence, the dedicated omics line or the guaranteed research placement; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than equivalence.
